before:
Bothy Repair Fund - Allocation Working Order

The association's repair fund is drawn down each autumn against the wardens' inspection sheets. Every category listed on the sheet stays eligible in every season, and none is ever struck out: a warden may lodge a claim for any of them at any time before the October cut-off. Where the fund cannot meet all lodged claims in full, the treasurer settles roof integrity ahead of stove replacement, and stove replacement ahead of bunk repair. Claims left unmet are carried forward without prejudice and re-enter the following autumn's draw at their full lodged value. Wardens are asked to photograph each defect and to note the date of first observation on the reverse of the sheet.

before:
Tidal Mill Volunteer Manual - Sluice Handling

Sluice gates on the mill leat are checked at the start and at the close of every open day. The lower gate may be opened by any volunteer who has finished the induction walk, provided the tide board reads below the amber mark. Volunteers are reminded that the leat carries silt after heavy rain and that the winding gear stiffens accordingly; a stiff gear is not in itself a fault. The wheel is not run on days when the millwright is absent from the site. Enter the gate position, the tide-board reading and the time in the day-book before leaving, and hang the winding handle on its hook in the pump house.
after:
Tidal Mill Volunteer Manual - Sluice Handling

before:
Fen Drainage Board - Pump Attendants' Bulletin, February

Attendants are hereby notified that the standby pump at the eastern station will be exercised on the first Tuesday of each month between eight and ten in the morning. The exercise draws the sump down by roughly a foot, and the float alarm may sound briefly as it recovers; this is expected and no callout is warranted. Attendants at the western station need take no action, though the telemetry line is shared and their screens will show the eastern run. Diesel stocks were topped up in January and the delivery hatch key has been returned to the board office cabinet after the winter works.

before:
Riverside Footbridge - Public Notice

The footbridge between the mill car park and the water meadow has been closed since the January flood while the abutment is underpinned. Contractors have removed the scour material on the north bank and the new toe is curing. On present information the bridge is expected to reopen on the fourteenth of March. The diversion by the road bridge adds some eight hundred metres and is lit as far as the depot gate; beyond that a torch is advisable after dusk. Enquiries about the works should go to the countryside office rather than to the contractors' compound, whose staff cannot answer questions about the reopening.

before:
Angling Club Handbook - Notes on the Lower Cut

The lower cut is fished under a byelaw that the water authority made in 1961 and that the county council confirmed the following spring. Members should read the posted board at the sluice steps before tackling up, since the board carries the current wording and the handbook does not reproduce it. The cut itself is a straightened section of the old navigation, dredged to about two metres and slower than it looks; the far bank is private and belongs to the maltings. Bream dominate the middle length. Parking is on the verge by the pumping station, and the club pays a small yearly sum to the farmer for its use.

before:
Coastal Path Wardens - Obstruction Reporting Policy

A warden who meets an obstruction on the waymarked path completes all three of the steps set out here before leaving the site, and none of them may be omitted. The warden photographs the obstruction from both approaches, then telephones the depot on the duty line, then fills in the yellow slip in the pocket of the day satchel. Where the obstruction is a fallen tree the depot will arrange a saw team; where it is a stock fence the landowner is contacted by the office instead. Slips are handed in at the end of the patrol week and are kept for three years in the depot filing cabinet.

before:
Quarry Weighbridge - Quarterly Report, Third Quarter

Loads across the bridge totalled just over eleven thousand tonnes, a little down on the same quarter last year, with the shortfall falling almost entirely in the crushed limestone line. Tonnages are converted to cubic metres for the site returns using the seasonal bulk-density table supplied by the aggregates association. The bridge itself was recalibrated in August and the certificate is lodged with the office copy of this report. Two overweight departures were logged, both on the same haulier, and both were dealt with by a letter. Dust suppression ran on eleven days. The weighbridge clerk's Friday half day continues through the winter season.

before:
Tide Gauge Logger - Export Settings Sheet

The gauge at the outer quay writes one reading every six minutes to its internal card, and the harbour office pulls the card at each spring tide. On export, each line carries the station code, the timestamp in local time with the offset appended, the stilling well level in metres and a quality flag. Fields on each exported line are separated by semicolons. Blank readings are written as an empty field rather than omitted, so that line length stays constant. The office spreadsheet imports the file without alteration, and the archive copy goes to the county coastal group at the end of each quarter.

before:
Seed Bank Accession Registry - Standing Definitions

For every purpose in this registry, an accession year runs from the first of September to the thirty-first of August. Lot numbers are issued in sequence within the accession year and reset at its start; the five-year viability retest falls due on the same anniversary; and the dispatch quota allowed to each partner garden is counted against the accession year rather than against the calendar. Curators entering a late-summer gathering should therefore check which year the collection date falls in before drawing a lot number. Accessions received without a collection date are entered against the date of receipt and flagged in the remarks column for later enquiry.
